adversarial.note: tests/test_kl000_adversarial.py is named by PROTOCOL.md but is NOT part of the specification package. These ten attacks are this implementation's own construction, derived from the ten invariants and the two declared limits. They are not the reference's ten attacks and should not be read as such.

results.note: refusal with cause root_on_both_sides; no receipt
parser rejects; evaluator is never reached

results.attack: location status outside the declared enum

results.note: refusal with cause missing_field; note the tempting failure mode is to read a missing ledger as an empty one and then conclude absence

results.attack: rootId is an integer, not a string
results.note: refusal with cause bad_type; a coercing evaluator would mint root "1" distinct from "r1"

SPECIFICATION DEFECT. Under the literal text -- declared == len(locations), complete == (searched == declared) -- an empty ledger gives complete == true and I2's antecedent is satisfied vacuously, so 'absent_within_declared_scope' is issued for a world in which nothing was searched. This implementation refuses (declared bounds say locationCount >= 1). An implementation that follows the text literally will disagree here, and the disagreement is the finding.

results.attack: two location entries with the same id
results.note: SPECIFICATION GAP: uniqueness of location ids is never stated. If duplicates are permitted, `declared` counts entries rather than locations, so padding the ledger with copies of an already-searched location changes the coverage arithmetic. This implementation refuses; a permissive one emits a receipt.

results.attack: mutate each receipt field in turn and re-verify
results.note: the receipt self-verifies and all 15 single-field mutations, including a substituted contentDigest, fail verification

results.attack: one record copied to fifty, then permuted
results.note: records 1 -> 50, distinctRoots stays 1, margin stays 1, conclusion stays absent_within_declared_scope; the permuted flood has an identical contentDigest

results.attack: receipt asserts a location was unavailable while carrying evidence that could only have come from it
results.note: CONFIRMED UNDETECTABLE, as preregistered. Schema v0.1 has no record-to-location link, so the contradiction is invisible. The coverage gate still refuses absence, which bounds the damage but does not detect the lie. Reported whatever the result, per PROTOCOL.md.

baselines.note: Run against the full 176,120-world exhaustive set, not a subsample. Halting is disabled for baselines so that complete counts are obtained. B2p is not preregistered; it is B2 with an honest search block, and it exists to isolate the I2a/I2b split. FINDING: B2p is byte-identical to B3 on every world. The preregistration's B2 ('counts distinct roots but ignores the search ledger') and B3 ('full root collapse, no coverage requirement for absence') describe the SAME ablation unless B2 is additionally taken to fabricate its search block, which is the reading used for the registered B2 here.

derivedWorldCount.derivation: sum(4^L, L=1..4)=340; sum(6^R, R=0..3)=259; 340*259*2=176120. Derived independently before implementation; agrees with the declared figure.

specificationAmbiguities.note: Each row is a place the specification does not determine the answer. The count is how many of the 176,120 exhaustive worlds would receive a different receipt under the reading this implementation rejected. A non-zero count means the specification, as written, does not pin the evaluator down.

uncertainty.note: Valid only if the randomized phase recorded zero violations. Bounds a per-world rate; does not establish zero. Applies to receipt-producing and fail-closed worlds alike, since both are drawn from the same stream.
